questions.prompt: Explain why Universal Links are more secure than custom URL schemes like myapp:// in 2 to 5 sentences.

rubric.description: Explains that custom schemes can be hijacked by any malicious app registering the same scheme.
Explains that Universal Links use two-way cryptographic verification via apple-app-site-association.
Mentions that Universal Links fall back safely to Safari when the app is not installed.

questions.modelAnswer: Universal Links prevent scheme hijacking through a two-way cryptographic verification between the domain and the app. Any installed application can register the same custom URL scheme and intercept sensitive tokens. In contrast, Universal Links require hosting an apple-app-site-association file that proves domain ownership. If the application is not installed, Universal Links fall back safely to your website in Safari.

sources.title: Supporting universal links in your app (Xcode)

questions.prompt: Describe the role and requirements of the apple-app-site-association file in 2 to 5 sentences.

rubric.description: Explains that the file maps allowed URL paths to specific app bundle IDs and team IDs.
States that the file must reside in the .well-known folder or root directory over HTTPS.
Specifies that the server must return HTTP 200 without redirects using application/json MIME type.

questions.modelAnswer: The apple-app-site-association file defines which web paths your application handles. It must be served over HTTPS directly from the domain root or the .well-known directory. The web server must return HTTP status 200 without redirects. It must use the application/json MIME type and link your Apple Team ID and bundle ID to specific path components.

questions.prompt: Explain how SwiftUI and UIKit receive and process deep links in 2 to 5 sentences.

rubric.description: States that SwiftUI uses the onOpenURL modifier attached to a top-level view.
Explains that UIKit scenes receive Universal Links in scene continue userActivity with web browsing type.
Mentions parsing the incoming URL path and query items to update navigation state.

questions.modelAnswer: SwiftUI handles deep links using the onOpenURL modifier attached to a top-level view. In modern UIKit scene-based apps, Universal Links arrive through scene continue userActivity with NSUserActivityTypeBrowsingWeb. Custom schemes in UIKit arrive via scene openURLContexts. Both frameworks parse the incoming URL components to update navigation state and display the target screen.

questions.prompt: Describe two common pitfalls when testing Universal Links and how to avoid them in 2 to 5 sentences.

rubric.description: Explains that pasting links into Safari address bar loads the web page, requiring testing via Notes or Messages.
Identifies server issues like HTTP redirects or invalid SSL certificates that cause Apple CDN rejection.

questions.modelAnswer: One common pitfall is pasting the URL directly into the Safari address bar, which forces Safari to load the website instead of the native app. Developers should test links by tapping them inside Notes, Mail, or Messages. Another pitfall is serving the association file with HTTP redirects or self-signed certificates, which Apple CDN rejects. Developers should verify the file returns HTTP 200 over a valid HTTPS domain.

rubric.description: Explains that the app buffers or queues the parsed route rather than discarding it.
Explains that the app replays the buffered link to navigate to the target screen after authentication finishes.

questions.modelAnswer: The app should avoid discarding deep links when a user is not logged in. Instead, a deep link coordinator parses and buffers the destination route in memory or secure storage. The user is first presented with the login or onboarding flow. Once authentication succeeds, the coordinator retrieves the buffered route and completes navigation to the intended screen.
